requirements.quote:
QUIC does not use
   TLS early data.
requirements.condition: When carrying early data with QUIC.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the QUIC 0-RTT mechanism rather than TLS early-data records.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using TLS early data directly in QUIC.
requirements.why_checkable: The TLS integration and wire encoding can be inspected for use of TLS early-data records.

requirements.quote: QUIC uses 0-RTT packets to carry early data.
requirements.condition: When a QUIC endpoint carries early data.
requirements.required_behavior: Carry the early data in QUIC 0-RTT packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Carrying QUIC early data in another packet type.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet traces can correlate early application data with the 0-RTT packet type.

requirements.quote:
Accordingly, the max_early_data_size parameter is repurposed to hold
   a sentinel value 0xffffffff to indicate that the server is willing to
   accept QUIC 0-RTT data.
requirements.condition: When a server indicates willingness to accept QUIC 0-RTT data in a NewSessionTicket.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the early_data extension with max_early_data_size set to the sentinel value 0xffffffff.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using max_early_data_size as a byte-count value for QUIC 0-RTT acceptance.
requirements.why_checkable: A decoded NewSessionTicket can be checked for the extension and exact 32-bit sentinel value.

requirements.quote:
To indicate that the server does not accept
   0-RTT data, the early_data extension is omitted from the
   NewSessionTicket.
requirements.condition: When a server indicates that it does not accept 0-RTT data.
requirements.required_behavior: Omit the early_data extension from the NewSessionTicket.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Including the early_data extension while indicating that 0-RTT is not accepted.
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized NewSessionTicket can be checked for absence of the extension.

requirements.quote:
The amount of data that the client can send in
   QUIC 0-RTT is controlled by the initial_max_data transport parameter
   supplied by the server.
requirements.condition: When a client sends data in QUIC 0-RTT.
requirements.required_behavior: Limit the amount sent according to the server-supplied initial_max_data transport parameter.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending QUIC 0-RTT data beyond the server-supplied initial_max_data limit.
requirements.why_checkable: A client test can compare cumulative 0-RTT data with the remembered initial_max_data value.

requirements.quote:
Servers MUST NOT send the early_data extension with a
   max_early_data_size field set to any value other than 0xffffffff.
requirements.condition: When a server sends an early_data extension in a NewSessionTicket.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending the extension with max_early_data_size set to any other value.
requirements.why_checkable: The field value is directly observable in an encoded NewSessionTicket.

requirements.quote:
A
   client MUST treat receipt of a NewSessionTicket that contains an
   early_data extension with any other value as a connection error of
   type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.condition: When a client receives a NewSessionTicket whose early_data extension has max_early_data_size other than 0xffffffff.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Accepting or ignoring the invalid max_early_data_size value.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat receipt as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.why_checkable: A crafted NewSessionTicket can exercise the client and verify the exact connection error.

requirements.quote:
A client that wishes to send 0-RTT packets uses the early_data
   extension in the ClientHello message of a subsequent handshake; see
   Section 4.2.10 of [TLS13].
requirements.condition: When a client wishes to send 0-RTT packets on a subsequent handshake.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the early_data extension in that handshake's ClientHello.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Attempting to send 0-RTT packets without using the ClientHello early_data extension.
requirements.why_checkable: A resumed-handshake trace can correlate a 0-RTT attempt with the ClientHello extension.

requirements.quote:
It then sends application data in 0-RTT
   packets.
requirements.condition: After a client signals a 0-RTT attempt with the ClientHello early_data extension.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the early application data in 0-RTT packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending that early application data in a non-0-RTT packet type.
requirements.why_checkable: A handshake packet trace can check the packet type containing early application data.
